set.body:
Per-unit anchor confidence in the Sherlock recall-to-video report.

A report row currently shows the MAP anchor and total source/external mass, so a downstream
consumer cannot tell a unit whose mass is concentrated on one row of the film from one whose
mass is spread over eight nominees. AlignmentRow already measures this - anchorMass,
localizability(sourceNodeCount), topK - and the runner publishes none of it.

Slice: report gains mapAnchorMass (mass on the MAP anchor, both modes summed), runnerUpAnchor
and runnerUpMass (second-best anchor by mass), and localizability (1 - H_source/log K over the
view's alignable nodes; empty cell when the unit has no source mass, per the method's own
absence contract - never imputed). All raw quantities; no thresholded "confident" boolean is
published, because any cutoff is the consumer's decision, not a measurement.

Evidence: unit test on a hand-built AlignmentRow (public AlignmentRow.of) with independently
computed expected values; end-to-end smoke assertions on the existing red-door fixture;
scoped gate on embed-bench.
set.title: Per-unit anchor confidence columns in the Sherlock recall report
